rv.q: This is a vastly better Chicago staging.

Directed by Jess McLeod and with a typically — meaning exceptionally — able Steppenwolf cast, 'The Thanksgiving Play' feels like a mix between the excellent sitcom 'Abbott Elementary,' the recent cringeworthy Showtime series 'The Curse,' and in theme, the work of Suzan-Lori Parks...
It’s a blistering send-up of how bleeding-heart white people can find themselves twisted in knots trying to appease political correctness, and at what cost.
This funny and unusually shocking production, much like Steppenwolf Theatre’s recent POTUS, is a play that will stick with theatergoers long after the final curtain call.
The Thanksgiving Play is a hilarious examination of the absurdity of human existence and interactions By Karen Topham May 11, 2024.
Fellow white theatergoers, if one must swallow a bitter pill – this is a pleasurable way to get it down.
Helming the play’s Chicago premiere fell to director Jess McLeod, whose canny, swiftly paced production benefits from an exceptional, indefatigable cast.
Although The Thanksgiving Play offers plenty of laughs, the play does not succeed as satire.
What this play attempts, with mixed but interesting results, is to show that mainstream white culture continues to do now what it did a century ago...
Ultimately, The Thanksgiving Play proves as exhausting as hearing a kid practice the same guitar chord again and again.
This is a laugh-out-loud play that will have you in stitches for the entire 90 minutes.
The way the story is told amidst it’s show-and-tell ambiance, coupled with the supreme energy of the actors is more than enough to carry the script.

cn.t: FastHorse's satire of well-meaning white liberals devising a politically correct Thanksgiving play earns mostly positive reviews for its sharp humor and strong performances, though some critics find the one-joke premise repetitive and lacking wit.
